findings.title: New-client snapshots and EntityManager state reads go stale on the GPU path
findings.description: The design's A3 claims "Downstream code (`client_manager.broadcast`, sim logger) requires zero changes," but the world server has another consumer the design never accounts for: `make_snapshot_builder()` (`src/migratory_server/clients.py:344`) constructs `TickResult.from_numpy_state(em.state, em.count)` on every new client connection, reading the CPU `AgentState` arrays directly. On the GPU path the driver owns state; nothing in the design writes GPU results back to `AgentState`, so a client connecting mid-session receives a snapshot of the state as it was at server startup (or last spawn), not current positions. The same staleness applies to `EntityManager.get_position()` and any other direct `em.state` reader. The requirement left unmet: new clients must receive a snapshot reflecting current world state. The design needs to either (a) write back GPU state to `AgentState` per tick, (b) build snapshots from the GPU path's `TickResult`, or (c) explicitly document and accept snapshot staleness — currently it is silent on this, which is exactly the "hidden dependency" failure mode.

findings.title: No-GPU fallback (A7) is unreachable as designed — `_select_arch()` contradicts the stated failure behavior
findings.description: `_select_arch()` selects by `platform.system()` only: every Linux host returns `qd.cuda`, every Darwin host returns `qd.metal`, regardless of whether the device exists. But the design's own Open Notes state "If `qd.init()` raises (e.g. CUDA driver absent, GPU OOM during field allocation), `GpuSimulationDriver.setup()` propagates the exception and the server exits at startup." These two statements contradict A7: "A host with no Metal and no CUDA starts successfully with `backend: quadrants` — `_select_arch()` falls back to `qd.cpu` and logs a WARNING." On a Linux host without an NVIDIA GPU, the design as written raises at `qd.init(arch=qd.cuda)` and exits — A7 can never pass. The requirement unmet: the architecture's failsafe ("quadrants backend on a host with no Metal or CUDA still runs correctly on `qd.cpu`, with a warning") and the slice's own Scope bullet ("falls back to CPU with a logged warning if neither is detected"). Fix: detect at init time (e.g., attempt the preferred arch, catch the init failure, fall back to `qd.cpu` with the warning), or restrict A7 to the unsupported-platform case and restate A7 to match.

findings.title: REFLECT velocity sync-back is missing — `notify_positions_modified` uploads positions only
findings.description: `apply_bounds_policy` (`src/migratory_server/bounds_enforcement.py`) mutates both positions and velocities under `BoundsPolicy.REFLECT` (velocity sign-flip is load-bearing for the bounce behavior). The sync-back mechanism the design specifies is `gpu_driver.notify_positions_modified(result.positions[:result.count])`, which stores and later uploads only positions. Under REFLECT, the flipped velocities are broadcast to clients but never reach the GPU state, so the next tick integrates from the pre-reflection velocity — the bounce is invisible to the simulation and the GPU and client trajectories diverge. The requirement unmet: A4 requires all four bounds policies to "produce valid positions after 100 ticks on the GPU path," and REFLECT's semantics require the velocity correction to persist. The interface should be `notify_state_modified(positions, velocities)` (or `upload_positions` + `upload_velocities`), with wrap uploading positions only and reflect uploading both.

findings.title: Count-based change detection misses equal-count mutations and GPU field capacity is unspecified for runtime growth
findings.description:
Two gaps in the spawn/despawn sync mechanism:
1. `count_changed_since_last_tick()` compares only the count. `EntityManager.remove_entity()` shifts array indices (`src/migratory_server/entities.py` rebuilds `_id_to_index` with `idx - 1`), so a despawn followed by a spawn between ticks leaves the count unchanged while positions/profile indices at shifted indices differ — the GPU state is silently stale. The requirement unmet: any mutation of entity state must trigger re-upload. Track a mutation counter (or generation number) rather than the count.
2. `GpuAgentState` fields are allocated once at `setup()` with `n = entity_manager.count` (Quadrants fields recompile on shape change; slice 145 notes the runner "allocates once and never resizes"). The design never states whether `sync_from_entity_manager()` handles a count *larger* than the allocated field size — an upload beyond the allocated N fails or truncates. `EntityManager.spawn_entity()` is a runtime API, so population growth past the setup-time count is a reachable path. The design must either allocate fields at `entity_manager.capacity` up front or specify reallocation on growth (and name the recompilation cost).

findings.title: f64-export claim contradicts the `GpuAgentState` implementation the design says it moves unchanged
findings.description: The design states: "`export_positions()` and `export_velocities()` return f64 arrays (Quadrants upcasts on download). The `TickResult` therefore carries f64, preserving the downstream contract." The actual implementation being moved (`src/migratory/bench/backends/quadrants_fused_state.py:242,253`) returns **f32** (`np.column_stack([x, y]).astype(np.float32)`), and `TickResult.from_quadrants_fields` (`src/migratory/engine/tick_result.py`) documents that "Slice 145 backends pass f32 positions/velocities here." The design also says the moved module gets "no logic changes." These cannot all be true: either the design adds an f32→f64 upcast per tick (a logic change to the export path, with a per-tick allocation cost at N=50k the design does not account for), or `TickResult` carries f32 and the "preserving the downstream contract" claim is wrong in dtype terms. The design must pick one and state the real dtype contract, because `apply_bounds_policy` and the wire encoder both sit downstream of this boundary.

findings.title: Server-teardown claim references a path that does not exist
findings.description: The design says "Shutdown: the existing server teardown path calls `simulation_manager` cleanup; add `gpu_driver.finalize()` there." There is no existing `simulation_manager` cleanup path in `server.py` — shutdown runs reverse-registered hooks and the `finally` block that shuts down the sim executor. The intent is clear, but the design should name the actual location (e.g., register a shutdown hook or extend the `finally` block after `self._sim_executor.shutdown(...)`), since `finalize()` calling `qd.reset()` must run before process exit on the GPU path.
